subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should the browser tool make compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals the default interaction contract, or keep the current capped snapshot behavior with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility boundaries rather than repairing one clearly broken code path.

options.title: Adopt Compact Browser Defaults
options.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

options.title: Keep Current Capped Behavior
options.body: Retain current AI snapshot caps and opt-in efficient mode, and treat additional browser compaction as future targeted improvements.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Context Work
options.body: Track this under broader context and tool-output compression architecture if maintainers do not want browser-specific defaults.

recommendation.title: Adopt Compact Browser Defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser snapshot default mode, bundled browser plugin boundary, and current browser docs history make this the strongest routing candidate for the product-contract choice.
